outline.description: This chapter introduces the parties, their respective businesses and marks, the procedural history before the USPTO and the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board, and the basis for the Federal Circuit's jurisdiction on appeal.
subtopics: CC Serve's business model and its registered ASPIRE word mark for credit card services
Apex Bank's business operations and its intent-to-use applications for ASPIRE BANK word and design marks
The letter of protest, publication for opposition, and CC Serve's opposition proceeding before the Board
The Board's decision sustaining the opposition under Section 2(d) of the Lanham Act
Apex's appeal to the Federal Circuit and the court's jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1295(a)(4)(B)

outline.chapter_title: Legal Framework: Likelihood of Confusion and the DuPont Factors
outline.description: This chapter explains the legal standard for likelihood of confusion under Section 2(d) of the Lanham Act, the thirteen DuPont factors, the nature of the likelihood-of-confusion inquiry as a legal conclusion based on factual findings, and the standards of appellate review applied by the Federal Circuit.
subtopics: Section 2(d) of the Lanham Act and the prohibition on registration when confusion is likely from concurrent use of marks
The thirteen DuPont factors and the Board's discretion to consider only those that are relevant and of record
Likelihood of confusion as a question of law based on underlying factual findings under the DuPont factors
De novo review of the Board's legal conclusions and substantial evidence review of its factual findings
The scope of Apex's appeal: challenges to the Board's analysis of the first, second, and sixth DuPont factors

outline.chapter_title: The Second DuPont Factor: Similarity of the Parties' Goods and Services
outline.description: This chapter examines the Board's analysis of the second DuPont factor, which assesses the similarity of the parties' services. It covers the legal standard for service similarity, the Board's methodology for comparing credit card services with banking and financing services, Apex's arguments on appeal, and the Federal Circuit's affirmance based on substantial evidence.
subtopics: The legal standard for the second DuPont factor: services need not be identical but related in a way that could cause mistaken belief of common source
The Board's determination of the scope of 'credit card services' after deletion from the Trademark ID Manual
The Board's finding that the parties' services are 'legally identical, in part' based on dictionary definitions and third-party registrations
Apex's argument that CC Serve merely partners with banks rather than providing banking services itself
The Federal Circuit's affirmance: substantial evidence supports the Board's finding of high similarity between the parties' services

outline.chapter_title: The Sixth DuPont Factor: Number and Nature of Similar Marks in Use on Similar Goods
outline.description: This chapter details the legal error the Board committed in analyzing the sixth DuPont factor. It explains the role of third-party mark evidence in demonstrating mark weakness, the Board's improper narrowing of the relevant universe of marks to only those for credit card services, and the Federal Circuit's reasoning that the Board's similarity standard must be consistent across DuPont factors.
subtopics: The legal purpose of the sixth DuPont factor: third-party use of similar marks on similar goods as evidence of mark weakness and consumer education to distinguish marks
Apex's evidence of third-party ASPIRE and ASPIRE-formative marks across financial services
The Board's restriction of relevant marks to only credit card services and its exclusion of other banking and financing marks
The Board's finding that nine marks do not rise to the level of 'considerable' or 'ubiquitous' use sufficient to demonstrate weakness
The Federal Circuit's legal error analysis: the Board applied an inconsistent and overly narrow definition of similarity under factor six compared to factor two
The principle that the Board must maintain the same scope of similarity across DuPont factors when it has already found services to be highly similar or partially legally identical
Vacation and remand for reconsideration of the appropriate scope of third-party marks eligible for consideration

outline.chapter_title: The First DuPont Factor and Overall Disposition
outline.description: This chapter explains the first DuPont factor's focus on the similarity of the marks in their entireties, the dependency of the commercial impression analysis on the outcome of the sixth factor's reconsideration, and the court's ultimate disposition of affirming the second factor while vacating and remanding the first and sixth factors.
subtopics: The first DuPont factor: similarity of marks in their entireties as to appearance, sound, connotation, and commercial impression
The relationship between commercial strength (informed by the sixth factor) and commercial impression (central to the first factor)
The Federal Circuit's reasoning that reconsideration of the sixth factor may alter the determination of the mark's commercial strength or weakness, affecting the first factor analysis

The court's disposition: affirm-in-part the second factor, vacate-in-part the first and sixth factors, and remand for reconsideration consistent with the Board's factual finding of high service similarity
Costs awarded to appellant and the practical significance of the decision for ensuring consistency across DuPont factor analyses
